belief: If I doubt, I'm a bad Christian.
origins: Many were taught that questions are sinful and faith means never wondering. Seasons of loss, unanswered prayer, or hard questions then bring fear and shame. People hide doubts and feel alone.
teaches: A father cried out to Jesus, “I do believe; help my unbelief!” and Jesus healed his son. Jude writes, “have mercy on those who doubt.” The Bereans “examined the Scriptures every day to see if these teachings were true,” and Luke calls them noble-minded. Hebrews says, “faith is the assurance of what we hope for and the certainty of what we do not see.” Doubt can be a doorway to deeper faith when we bring it to God and to Scripture instead of hiding it.
self_statements: My questions prove I do not believe.
God is angry at my doubts.
errors: Believing I either have perfect faith or none.
Assuming others would condemn my questions.
Feeling uncertain and concluding that my faith is gone.
Predicting I will lose my faith.
questions: How did Jesus respond to the father who admitted unbelief?
Who in Scripture asked hard questions of God?
What could I do to look for answers instead of hiding?
Who could I talk with who welcomes honest questions?
What do I still hold on to?
truth: Honest doubt brought to God is not a failure of faith. Jesus welcomes “I believe; help my unbelief.” I can ask questions, seek answers, and keep trusting.
hw_truths: God has mercy on those who doubt.
I can bring my questions to God.
I am not alone in doubt.
log: Each week, write one question and where you looked for an answer.
actions: Look up the question in Scripture or with a trusted pastor.
Share it with a wise believer.
prayer: Lord, I believe; help my unbelief. Thank You for welcoming my questions. Lead me to answers and keep me close to You. Amen.
name_example: Sarah can write: “I believe; help my unbelief.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “If I doubt, I'm a bad Christian.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
